text.title: Single Channel Bet Selector — Worked Example
text.summary: One complete channel-bet record for a solo founder selling ops-team tooling (11 paying customers, four tactic-level candidates, LinkedIn founder posts chosen at 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 with 7 of 11 customers observed there, a 90-day bet with 3 posts a week, week-4 and week-8 checkpoints and a kill criterion written on the selection day, three parked channels) with a note per value, plus a "social" bet from a Slack decision and what the validator prints.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: A solo founder sells a scheduling tool to operations managers at mid-size logistics firms. Eleven customers pay; none came from a channel the founder works deliberately. The founder has been posting on LinkedIn, sending some cold email, drafting SEO pages and hanging out in two Slack communities, all at once, for four months. Asked where they found the product, 7 of the 11 customers named a LinkedIn post; 3 unsolicited demo requests arrived through LinkedIn in the last quarter.

example.title: LinkedIn founder posts, 90 days from 2026-09-14
example.note: The rubric is dated and lives in the founder's decisions repository, so week 12 is graded against a written page rather than a memory (r-written-rubric-single-page). No channel produces a paying customer a month, and 11 customers clear the 5-customer sample bar (r-icp-density-cites-sample). Four candidates are written at the level of the weekly action and mapped to Traction's taxonomy; "social" or "outbound" could not be scored on founder fit (r-candidate-set-from-named-list). Each is scored on exactly three unweighted axes and the total is their sum (r-three-axis-scoring); every density score carries its observed-of-11 count, and the Slack communities score 2 because only 2 of 11 customers were seen there (r-icp-density-cites-sample). LinkedIn posts total 12 with no axis below 3 and is the only candidate that clears; cold email totals 8 with early traction at 2, so a strong founder fit could not rescue it (r-threshold-12-of-15-and-per-axis-floor). One channel, 2026-09-14 to 2026-12-13 (90 days), and the other three sit in the parking lot with their totals and no active work (r-one-channel-parking-lot). The weekly unit is 3 posts of a stated length; week 4 expects 400 profile visits a week and week 8 expects 4 demo requests, so a burned approach shows up in a month, not a quarter (r-weekly-unit-and-checkpoints). The kill criterion, written on the selection day, is fewer than 10 qualified demo requests and fewer than 1 new paying customer by the end date, after which the rubric is re-run with the result as early-traction evidence; it is not revised (r-precommitted-kill-criterion).

example.title: a social bet decided in Slack
example.note: What the validator prints: `rubric_location` slack is too short to be a path or URL (r-written-rubric-single-page); `icp_sample` matches neither 5 paying customers nor 50 conversations (r-icp-density-cites-sample); `candidates` has 2 items where 3 are required and "social" is a category, not a tactic (r-candidate-set-from-named-list); `icp_density` must be 1 when `icp_density_sample` is null (r-icp-density-cites-sample); `bet.weekly_unit.count` 0 below 1, `checkpoints` has 1 item and week 12 is not 4 or 8 (r-weekly-unit-and-checkpoints); `kill_criterion.action` must re-run the rubric and `revised` must be false (r-precommitted-kill-criterion); `parking_lot.active_work_allowed` must be false (r-one-channel-parking-lot). Once the schema violations are fixed the cross-field checks add: total 13 is not 5 + 5 + 2 = 12 and the candidate does not clear the bar with early_traction 2; the bet runs 122 days, not 90; the kill criterion was written on 2026-11-30, not the selection day; and the second candidate is missing from the parking lot.
